Browser DevTools mastery (used in every phase) · 6/6

Async frames link the call history

Synchronous frames only

  • onInput, line 5
  • Who started this fetch?

With async frames

  • onInput, line 5
  • async boundary: await fetch
  • onInput, line 4, query re

The async frames show which input event started the stale request.

The onInput function reads the box on line 3,

awaits getJSON on line 4, and calls render on line 5.

An XHR or fetch breakpoint with the text search?q= pauses

on line 12 when a request URL contains it.

It pauses twice: for re, then for react.

A line-of-code breakpoint on line 5 pauses for every response.

First react arrives, and query matches the box.

Then re arrives, but the box still says react.

A conditional breakpoint pauses only when its condition is true.

With query !== input.value, it skips the fresh react

response and stops on the stale re response.

Step into enters render,

so render goes on top of the Call Stack.

Step over runs one line.

Step out finishes render and returns to onInput.

After an await, the stack holds only the resumed code.

Async frames link it back to the code that started the fetch,

so the Call Stack shows the whole history.
